title: Become a Better Reader
summary: Five tricks to understand and remember what you read.

steps.title: Look before you read
sentences: Look at the title, the headings and the pictures first.
Ask yourself what you already know about the topic.
This gives your brain a map of what is coming.

steps.title: Ask questions
sentences: As you read, ask who, what, where, when, why and how.
Stop after each paragraph and say it in your own words.
If you cannot, read it again more slowly.
points: Say it in your own words

steps.title: Unknown words
sentences: When you meet a new word, look at the words around it for clues.
Look for parts you know, like a prefix or root.
Then check a dictionary and write the word with an example sentence.

steps.title: Remember it
sentences: After reading, write three main points or draw a quick picture.
Tell the story to someone else.
Reading a little every day is better than a lot once a week.

facts: Reading for just 20 minutes a day means you read well over a million words in a year.
Reading aloud helps younger readers with pronunciation and understanding.
Libraries, including free public libraries, can lend you books at no cost.

quiz.q: What should you do before reading?
options: Look at the title and headings

quiz.q: What can you do with a new word?
options: Look for clues in the sentence
